scenes.title: Four degrees
scenes.purpose: Hook: the pitched visual. Show normal, then one tile warming and the colour spreading until the whole grid is hot. Date and place, then the line that nobody broke in.
scenes.visual: A grid of 8 x 14 fridge-door tiles on a cool white sheet, each a mono readout (4 on chilled, -18 on frozen, ultramarine). The room-tone compressor hum plays. One tile ticks 4, 5, 6 and the hum cuts out. A wave of colour spreads from that tile at constant speed, ultramarine to marigold to vermilion, until every tile is hot.

transition_out.continuity: one hot tile near the centre scales up to become the cutaway panel in s2

scenes.narration: Sunday night, October eleventh. Across France, supermarket fridges hummed at four degrees, freezers at eighteen below. By Monday, hundreds of stores were throwing everything out. Nobody had broken in. The machines had been told to warm up.

layout.portrait: Grid fills the upper two-thirds inside the safe area; mono date and place line above it; one copy line under the grid above the bottom UI safe zone.

beats.action: grid of cold tiles builds in a quick row-by-row cascade; compressor hum fades in
date typed in mono: SUN 11 OCT 2026 · France
one tile ticks 4, 5, 6; hum cuts out
colour wave leaves that tile and crosses the grid
grid is fully vermilion; copy line 'Nobody had broken in.' rises under it
one hot tile pulses as the match-cut target

scenes.title: A feature, not a bug
scenes.purpose: Explain defrost: every freezer does it on purpose; forcing it, for hours, is enough to spoil food.
scenes.visual: The hot tile opens into a flat cutaway of a freezer case: frost furring a coil. A heater glows marigold and the frost melts and drips. A small cycle timer shows a short arc, then a hand drags it out to a long one labelled 'reported: up to 8 h'. The food icons inside the case drift from ultramarine to vermilion while the arc fills.

transition_out.continuity: the cutaway panel shrinks back into one tile of the grid, now with a line running out of its back

scenes.narration: The weapon was a feature. Every freezer ices up, so it regularly heats its own coils to melt the frost. Normally that's a short cycle. This time defrost was forced on, and reports say some ran for eight hours.

layout.portrait: Cutaway in the upper two-thirds; cycle timer docked bottom-right of the art; copy and source line below.

beats.action: tile expands to the cutaway; coil drawn on with frost
heater element ignites; frost melts off the coil
cycle timer appears with a short arc and the label 'normal'
arc is dragged out to a long sweep; label 'forced: reportedly up to 8 h'
food icons inside warm from ultramarine to vermilion

scenes.title: The open door
scenes.purpose: Why it worked: a back-room controller with a web page on the open internet, many of them old. Be honest about what is documented and what is not confirmed.
scenes.visual: The tile now shows a small controller box behind the fridges. A thin line runs from it up to a field of dots; the dots multiply to a scatter labelled '2,765 exposed (one model, Claroty scan)'. A daily code stamps onto the controller screen from today's date, then an ink question mark wobbles beside the controller: 'used here? unconfirmed'. A 'no security updates' tag stamps on old models.

transition_out.continuity: the field of dots becomes the next scene's grid of tiles, now empty

scenes.narration: Behind the cases sits a controller with its own web page, and in many stores it faced the open internet. DAN-foss says most affected units were old models with no security updates. Researchers had already found a hidden daily password, built from the date. Whether that exact flaw was used is unconfirmed.

layout.portrait: Controller box low-centre of the art area with the exposed-dot field filling the area above it; stamps on the controller screen; source line 'Claroty Team82; Danfoss via Reuters/AFP' in mono below the copy.

beats.action: controller box draws on in the back room of the tile
line runs out to the sky; dots appear along it and spread into a field
counter rolls to 2,765 exposed with the Claroty source line
'no security updates' tag stamps onto the controller
daily code types onto the screen, built from a date; calendar glyph beside it
marigold question mark over 'used here?'; it does not resolve

scenes.title: Hours in the dark
scenes.purpose: The damage: temperatures, fires, why the food had to go, and the scale with its source.
scenes.visual: A hero thermometer numeral in Playfair counts 4 to 50 in the top third; a mono timeline underneath marks 'about 6 h'. A single tile spikes to 80 and is circled. A horizontal rule marks 5° and a doubling-bacteria note stamps beside it. Tiles in the grid empty to outlines one by one. A bar of 700 highlighted tiles against 10,000 total fills at the end.

transition_out.continuity: the grid of emptied tiles shrinks to a corner dot of the next scene's map

scenes.narration: The alarms were reportedly silenced, so staff found out at opening. Cases reached about fifty degrees. One store reported eighty. Some equipment caught fire. Above five degrees, bacteria multiply fast, so it all went. France's economy minister cited about seven hundred stores.

layout.portrait: Hero numeral in the top third; grid in the middle third; 700-of-10,000 bar and source line in the copy zone.

beats.action: alarm bell glyph drawn, then struck through; 'reportedly silenced'
hero numeral counts 4 to 50; 'about 6 h' on the mono timeline
one tile spikes to 80 and is circled; a small flame glyph beside it
5° rule slides across the grid; 'bacteria multiply fast' stamps
tiles empty to outline one by one
bar fills: about 700 of about 10,000, with source

scenes.title: Again
scenes.purpose: The second wave: same method, several countries, and a fix that is more than an update.
scenes.visual: The grid dissolves into a tile-grid map of Europe in the same tile language (each country a tile, France already vermilion). A thin timeline stamps the two Sundays three weeks apart. Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and Ireland light up on their spoken cues, then Netherlands, Estonia and Finland as 'others'. A 'software update + physical change' chip pair replaces the timeline.

transition_out.continuity: the map's dots resolve back into the full grid for the closing scene

scenes.narration: Three weeks later, another Sunday night. Belgium, LUK-sem-burg, Sweden, Ireland and others reported the same pattern. A Belgian refrigeration firm says a real fix needs new software and a physical change to the unit.

layout.portrait: Map in the upper two-thirds; two-date timeline docked beneath it; fix label and source in the copy zone.

beats.action: corner dot expands into a dot-map of Europe
timeline draws with the Oct 11 stamp, then 'SUN 1 NOV 2026'
countries light up in turn as tiles warm
'others' dots warm in a short grid-wave
fix label draws on: software update + physical change

scenes.title: Who, and what now
scenes.purpose: No attribution; the three official steps; one closing idea; end hold.
scenes.visual: The full grid returns hot at 70% scale. The centre tile flips to an ink-outlined '?' tile (the temperature ramp stays reserved for temperature). Two quote cards appear and clear, then three checklist lines write on beside the officials' advice. The grid then cools back to ultramarine in a reverse wave and the closing line holds with the cold grid for the last 2.4 s.
scenes.narration: Nobody has claimed it. One expert said it could be kids messing around; governments have the skills too. Officials' advice is plain: take controllers off the internet, update the firmware, check the defrost schedule. When the thermostat is online, so is the food supply.
on_screen_text: When the thermostat is online, so is the food supply.

layout.portrait: Grid top two-thirds; checklist in the copy zone; closing line on its own line above the bottom UI safe zone, held for the last 2.5 s.
